policies.title: South Korean ordinary passports: Côte d’Ivoire preapproved arrival visa
policies.summary: Korean MFA requires an approved eVisa pre-enrolment document before departure for ordinary Korean passports. Côte d’Ivoire’s recognised official service prints and issues the biometric visa at Abidjan airport.
conditions: Applies to a valid ordinary Republic of Korea passport for a short visitor trip; diplomatic, official, service, residence, work, transit and final-admission rules are outside this finding.
Complete the approved online pre-enrolment before boarding and carry the approved response, payment receipt, passport and other listed entry documents.
At Abidjan airport, complete biometric enrolment; the visa is printed and issued there. This is advance electronic preapproval followed by arrival issuance, not electronic visa issuance.

application.label: Côte d’Ivoire official eVisa pre-enrolment
steps: Submit the ordinary-passport pre-enrolment and payment online.
Receive the approved pre-enrolment response before boarding.
Complete biometric enrolment at Abidjan airport, where the visa is printed and issued.

policies.title: South Korean ordinary passports: Eswatini visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Korea MFA’s current Eswatini entry panel states that ordinary Republic of Korea passport holders are visa-free for up to 60 days under the stated arrangement.
conditions: The entry panel states a 30-day visa-free stay, extendable by a further 30 days after entry, for a maximum stated 60 days.
This is limited to the ordinary short-visitor baseline; work, residence, special documents, extension approval and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: South Korean ordinary passports: Grenada visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Korea MFA’s current Grenada entry panel states that ordinary Republic of Korea passport holders have an agreement-based visa waiver for 90 days.
conditions: The stated maximum short stay is 90 days under the agreement-based waiver.
This is limited to ordinary passports and short visits; non-tourist purposes, special documents and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: South Korean ordinary passports: Mali advance mission visa
policies.summary: Korea MFA’s current Mali entry panel says ordinary Republic of Korea passport holders must obtain a visa in advance through the Malian Embassy in Japan or another competent mission.
conditions: Obtain the visa before travel through the Malian Embassy in Japan or another competent Malian mission.
The MFA warns that a traveller without a visa may be refused boarding or entry.
This is limited to ordinary short visitors; diplomatic and official passports, work, residence, transit and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: South Korean ordinary passports: Trinidad and Tobago visa-free short visit
policies.summary: Korea MFA’s current Trinidad and Tobago entry panel states that ordinary Republic of Korea passport holders have an agreement-based 90-day visa waiver.
conditions: The stated maximum short stay is 90 days under the agreement-based waiver.
This is limited to ordinary passports and short visits; non-tourist purposes, special documents and final admission remain separate.

conflicts.explanation: Korean MFA directly maps ordinary Korean passports to pre-enrolment before departure, while the Côte d’Ivoire official service prints and issues the biometric visa at Abidjan airport. The snapshot’s eVisa label misstates actual issuance timing.

unresolved.reason: The live Korean panel says ordinary passports are neither visa-free nor arrival-visa eligible, but Korea’s full travel prohibition and no demonstrated operative Afghan issuance channel prevent a normal visitor-status classification.

No current Korean, British Virgin Islands or United Kingdom authority source directly maps an ordinary Republic of Korea passport to a nationality-wide short-visitor route and issuance timing. Conditional territory or third-document rules are excluded.

The live Korean panel excludes ordinary passport visa-free and arrival-visa treatment, but does not establish whether the required visitor instrument is electronically or mission issued. A portal label cannot fill that issuance-timing gap.

The live Korean panel says arrival visas are not issued and visa-less arrivals are refused, but identifies no actual advance mission or electronic issuance route for an ordinary Korean visitor. Do not turn that incomplete timing evidence into a policy.

The live Korean panel says arrival visas are not issued and visa-less arrivals are refused, but identifies no actual advance mission or electronic issuance route for an ordinary Korean visitor. The fallback remains unconfirmed.

Korean MFA's live panel says arrival visas are issued, while Djibouti's current E-Government guidance says eVisa replaces the point-of-entry visa. No current direct source reconciles that issuance conflict for Korean ordinary passports.

The live Korean panel says ordinary passport holders without a visa are refused and arrival visas are not issued, but it does not prove the actual advance issuance channel. No complement or portal route is inferred.

The live Korean panel excludes ordinary-passport visa-free and arrival issuance but identifies both an embassy insurance application and an eVisa link without a Korean eligibility or issuance result. Those routes cannot safely be normalized.

Korean MFA directly describes an ordinary-passport eVisa route and emailed visa file, but Iraq is a Korean travel-prohibition destination and regional arrival procedures diverge. The combined legal and operational situation is not a normalizable baseline.

The live Korean panel records suspension of the ordinary-passport waiver, but no current direct Korean or Liberian authority source establishes the actual ordinary visitor issuance route. Mission-availability-dependent arrival options are not passport-wide evidence.

The live Korean panel excludes visa-free and arrival treatment and reports Niger's 2025 valid-visa rule, but it does not establish an actual ordinary Korean advance issuance channel. Do not infer one from a general application-document notice.
No current official source establishes a normal ordinary Republic of Korea short-visitor route for North Korea. Inter-Korean permissions, closure and Korean travel controls are not taxonomy statuses.

Palestinian access depends on Israeli-controlled crossings, permits, identity records and route-specific conditions. No current source establishes one Palestine-wide ordinary Korean-passport visitor status.

The current SLID-authenticated eVisa service covers a broad non-ECOWAS cohort but gives contradictory electronic-delivery and airport-or-border issuance statements. No current Korean-specific source resolves actual issuance timing.

Korean MFA records a travel prohibition. Its entry panel adds that an airport Entry Visa depends on a pre-issued Sudanese Entry Permit, creating conditional document and operational ambiguity rather than a normal visitor baseline.
Korean MFA's panel excludes visa-free and arrival issuance, but Korea's travel prohibition and the absence of a current direct ordinary-passport issuance route prevent normalization.

The live Korean panel permits airport issuance only with an approved official invitation; tourist invitations are travel-agency mediated and can be difficult to obtain. This invitation-conditioned route is outside the nationality-wide baseline.

The live Korean panel gives a 90-day ordinary-passport waiver but Ukraine is a Korean travel-prohibition destination. The combined legal and operational result cannot be represented as one normal visitor status.
